title: Harmonic phases reject symmetric smearing in 9 of 42 selected TESS CPVs at a fourfold noise scale
abstract: We test whether symmetric phase smearing can explain changes in selected complex periodic variables (CPVs). A common template with arbitrary real harmonic transfers must preserve harmonic phase differences modulo pi after one phase shift. We give an exact interval test with explicit coefficient error bounds. We use 282 published sector 56 to 107 TESS curves from 126 on-target CPVs. At the source bin noise scale, 39 of 62 stars with informative pairs have an incompatible pair. At four times that noise scale, 9 of 42 stars remain incompatible, with 48 rejected pairs out of 284. Tightening period agreement to 0.1% leaves nine rejected stars. New candidates alone give four. At eight times the noise scale, only one star fails. A Gaussian disk model supplies a reference bound, but real noise, sampling, and selection prevent a calibrated false-positive claim. The test excludes symmetric broadening and power changes within the stated bounds. Uneven sampling, asymmetric smearing, multiple periods and processing remain possible. No material lifetime is measured. Original code, aggregate results, synthetic checks, input hashes and separate-scratch repeat steps are included. External record tables are excluded.

display.caption: Signed symmetric-filter test across sector separation and four assumed noise scales. Error bars are star-bootstrap intervals; selection and noise-model errors are excluded.

citations.reason: Three verified entries supply folded curves, labels and noise estimates.
Prior shape-memory study leaves within-sector smearing as an ambiguity. This test allows arbitrary signed harmonic power changes.
